hyps.why: At already-large learning rates Adam diverges or oscillates, so further increases hurt.
Tiny learning rates leave the network under-trained in 243 epochs, so increasing them gives large gains.
Reducing an unstable learning rate recovers accuracy, whereas reducing a moderate one is neutral or harmful.
Tiny batches already yield many noisy updates, so larger steps add instability rather than speed.
Large batches give few updates per epoch, so a larger step size compensates for slow convergence.
With a small learning rate, fewer updates per epoch leaves training further from convergence.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training at high learning rates.
Strong L2 penalties cause severe underfitting, while increases at tiny alpha are negligible.
Very narrow networks are capacity-limited, so widening helps much more than for already-wide networks.
Deeper ReLU networks are more prone to divergence and dead units at large learning rates.
